I updated the Kafka mesh proxy filter to preserve and forward message headers to upstream brokers, with correct ownership/error handling. All changes are in **source files only** (tests untouched).

### Files changed

**`produce_outbound_record.h`**
- Added `using Header = std::pair<absl::string_view, absl::string_view>;`
- Added `const std::vector<Header> headers_;` as the 5th member
- Updated the constructor signature to accept `const std::vector<Header>& headers`, with init order `{topic, partition, key, value, headers}`

**`upstream_kafka_client.h`** (`KafkaProducer` interface)
- Changed `send` to `void send(const ProduceFinishCbSharedPtr callback, const OutboundRecord& record)` and now includes the outbound-record header

**`upstream_kafka_client_impl.h`** (`LibRdKafkaUtils` + `RichKafkaProducer`)
- Added `convertHeaders(...)` and `deleteHeaders(...)` to the `LibRdKafkaUtils` interface
- Updated `RichKafkaProducer::send` to the new signature and added a `const LibRdKafkaUtils& utils_` member (needed at send time)

**`upstream_kafka_client_impl.cc`**
- Implemented `convertHeaders` (creates `RdKafka::Headers`, adds each entry, deletes and returns `nullptr` on failure) and `deleteHeaders` (plain `delete`)
- Added a long-lived default utils instance via `CONSTRUCT_ON_FIRST_USE` so the reference stored in `utils_` stays valid in production (tests inject their own)
- Rewrote `send` with the required error handling:
  - abort + `ProduceFinishCb` notify if `convertHeaders` returns `nullptr` (no `deleteHeaders` call)
  - `produce(...)` now passes headers → **10 arguments** (maps to the existing `RdKafka::Headers*` overload)
  - on produce failure: call `deleteHeaders` then notify
  - on success: no `deleteHeaders` (ownership transferred to librdkafka)

**`produce.cc`** — updated the call site to `producer.send(shared_from_this(), outbound_record)`.

**`produce_record_extractor.cc`** — instead of discarding headers, extracts each header key/value into a `std::vector<Header>` and passes it to `OutboundRecord`, ensuring key, value, and headers are preserved end-to-end (also required so the struct compiles).
